answer: Sybil resistance binds each identity to bonded collateral, so coordinated equivocation cannot be cheaply partitioned across aliases: if k identities sign conflicting histories, correlated penalties grow as O(k^2), while detection applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier to the swarm’s escrowed stake. Thus splitting authority into a cedar, thread, or jade identity offers no escape; shared control increases expected loss faster than voting power.
